course: AP Calculus - Limits, Derivatives, Integrals and Series
attribution: Original scope and sequence authored for the Luminfest Learning Harness, dedicated to the public domain under CC0.
scope: Structure only: concept titles, unit order and prerequisite intent. No third-party curriculum text is reproduced, and no restricted source is ingested.
description: The AP Calculus AB and BC course framework: limits and continuity, differentiation and its applications, integration and accumulation, differential equations, applications of integration, and (BC) parametric, polar, vector and series topics.

concepts.title: Estimating limits from graphs and tables
concepts.summary: A limit describes the value a function approaches, which need not equal its value at the point.

concepts.title: Defining limits and limit notation
concepts.summary: The formal definition makes "approaches" precise and distinguishes one-sided from two-sided limits.
prerequisites: Estimating limits from graphs and tables

concepts.title: Limit properties and algebraic techniques
concepts.summary: Limits combine by sum, product and quotient, and factoring or rationalising resolves indeterminate forms.

concepts.title: Limits at infinity
concepts.summary: Limits at infinity describe end behaviour, including horizontal asymptotes.

concepts.title: The squeeze theorem
concepts.summary: If a function is trapped between two others with the same limit, it has that limit too.

concepts.title: Continuity at a point
concepts.summary: A function is continuous when its limit exists, its value exists, and the two agree.

concepts.title: Types of discontinuity
concepts.summary: Removable, jump and infinite discontinuities differ in whether a limit exists.

concepts.title: The intermediate value theorem
concepts.summary: A continuous function on an interval takes every value between its endpoint values.

concepts.title: Average and instantaneous rate of change
concepts.summary: The average rate is a secant slope and the instantaneous rate is the limit of secant slopes.

concepts.title: The derivative as a limit
concepts.summary: The derivative is the limit of a difference quotient, which gives the slope of the tangent line.
prerequisites: Average and instantaneous rate of change

concepts.title: Differentiability and continuity
concepts.summary: Differentiable implies continuous, but continuity does not imply differentiability.

concepts.title: The power rule
concepts.summary: The derivative of x to the n is n times x to the n minus one.

concepts.title: Constant, sum and difference rules
concepts.summary: Derivatives distribute over sums and differences, and a constant differentiates to zero.

concepts.title: The product rule
concepts.summary: The derivative of a product is the first times the derivative of the second plus the second times the derivative of the first.

concepts.title: The quotient rule
concepts.summary: The derivative of a quotient follows a fixed numerator pattern over the denominator squared.

concepts.title: Derivatives of trigonometric functions
concepts.summary: Sine and cosine differentiate into each other with a sign change, and the rest follow.

concepts.title: Higher-order derivatives
concepts.summary: Repeated differentiation gives acceleration from velocity, and concavity from slope.

concepts.title: Tangent line approximation
concepts.summary: The tangent line gives a local linear approximation of a function.

strands.strand: Differentiation: Composite, Implicit and Inverse Functions

concepts.title: The chain rule
concepts.summary: The derivative of a composition multiplies the outer derivative by the inner derivative.

concepts.title: Implicit differentiation
concepts.summary: Differentiating both sides of a relation and treating y as a function of x gives dy by dx.

concepts.title: Derivatives of inverse functions
concepts.summary: The derivative of an inverse is the reciprocal of the original derivative at the corresponding point.

concepts.title: Derivatives of exponential functions
concepts.summary: The exponential function is its own derivative, and a base change brings down a factor.

concepts.title: Derivatives of logarithmic functions
concepts.summary: The natural logarithm differentiates to one over x, and the chain rule extends it.

concepts.title: Derivatives of inverse trigonometric functions
concepts.summary: Inverse trigonometric derivatives follow standard forms used in integration.

concepts.title: Logarithmic differentiation
concepts.summary: Taking a logarithm first turns products and powers into sums, which simplifies the derivative.

concepts.title: Selecting differentiation procedures
concepts.summary: Recognising the structure of an expression decides which rule applies.

concepts.title: Interpreting derivatives in context
concepts.summary: A derivative is a rate with units, and its sign reports direction of change.

concepts.title: Straight-line motion
concepts.summary: Position, velocity and acceleration are related by successive derivatives.

concepts.title: Related rates
concepts.summary: When two quantities are linked, differentiating the relation in time connects their rates.

concepts.title: Local linearity and approximation
concepts.summary: Near a point a differentiable function behaves like its tangent line.

concepts.title: L'Hôpital's rule
concepts.summary: Indeterminate limits of quotients can be evaluated by differentiating numerator and denominator.

concepts.title: The mean value theorem
concepts.summary: Somewhere in an interval the instantaneous rate equals the average rate.

concepts.title: The extreme value theorem
concepts.summary: A continuous function on a closed interval attains a maximum and a minimum.

concepts.title: Critical points
concepts.summary: Critical points are where the derivative is zero or undefined, and they candidate the extrema.

concepts.title: Increasing and decreasing intervals
concepts.summary: The sign of the derivative reports where a function rises or falls.

concepts.title: The first derivative test
concepts.summary: A sign change of the derivative identifies a local maximum or minimum.

concepts.title: Concavity and inflection points
concepts.summary: The sign of the second derivative reports concavity and where it changes.

concepts.title: The second derivative test
concepts.summary: The second derivative classifies a stationary point as a maximum or a minimum.

concepts.title: Optimisation problems
concepts.summary: A constraint reduces a quantity to one variable, and the derivative locates its optimum.

concepts.title: Connecting graphs of f, f prime and f double prime
concepts.summary: The signs and zeros of the first two derivatives describe the shape of the function.

concepts.title: Riemann sums
concepts.summary: A definite integral is the limit of sums of rectangular areas.

concepts.title: The definite integral as a limit
concepts.summary: The integral is defined as a limit of Riemann sums, which makes accumulation precise.

concepts.title: The fundamental theorem of calculus
concepts.summary: Differentiation and integration are inverse processes, which links area to antiderivatives.
prerequisites: The definite integral as a limit

concepts.title: Antiderivatives and indefinite integrals
concepts.summary: An antiderivative reverses differentiation, up to an additive constant.

concepts.title: Properties of definite integrals
concepts.summary: Integrals split, reverse sign and combine linearly, which simplifies evaluation.

concepts.title: Accumulation functions
concepts.summary: An accumulation function's derivative is the integrand, which lets integrals be differentiated.

concepts.title: Integration by substitution
concepts.summary: Substitution reverses the chain rule and simplifies many integrals.

concepts.title: Integration by parts
concepts.summary: Integration by parts reverses the product rule.

concepts.title: Partial fractions
concepts.summary: A rational integrand can be split into simpler fractions that integrate directly.

concepts.title: Improper integrals
concepts.summary: An integral over an infinite interval or with a singularity is defined by a limit and may diverge.

concepts.title: Modelling with differential equations
concepts.summary: A differential equation states how a quantity changes in terms of the quantity itself.

concepts.title: Slope fields
concepts.summary: A slope field draws the derivative at each point, which reveals solution curves.

concepts.title: Separation of variables
concepts.summary: Separating the variables allows each side to be integrated independently.

concepts.title: Exponential models
concepts.summary: A rate proportional to the amount gives exponential growth or decay.

concepts.title: Logistic models
concepts.summary: A rate limited by a carrying capacity gives logistic growth.

concepts.title: Average value of a function
concepts.summary: The average value is the integral over the interval divided by the interval length.

concepts.title: Area between curves
concepts.summary: Area between curves is the integral of the upper minus the lower function.

concepts.title: Volumes with known cross sections
concepts.summary: Integrating the area of a cross section gives the volume of a solid.

concepts.title: Volumes of revolution: disk and washer
concepts.summary: Rotating a region about an axis gives circular cross sections, with the washer handling a gap.

concepts.title: Volumes of revolution: shell method
concepts.summary: Cylindrical shells integrate along the axis perpendicular to the one used by disks.
prerequisites: Volumes of revolution: disk and washer

concepts.title: Arc length
concepts.summary: Arc length integrates the length element derived from the Pythagorean theorem.

concepts.title: Accumulated change in context
concepts.summary: The integral of a rate gives the total change in the underlying quantity.

topics.topic: Curves beyond y equals f of x

concepts.title: Parametric equations and derivatives
concepts.summary: Parametric curves describe x and y separately, and dy by dx is the ratio of their derivatives.

concepts.title: Motion with parametric and vector functions
concepts.summary: Velocity and acceleration become vector quantities with direction and magnitude.

concepts.title: Polar coordinates
concepts.summary: Polar coordinates locate a point by distance and angle, and they convert to and from Cartesian.
prerequisites: Motion with parametric and vector functions

concepts.title: Area and arc length in polar coordinates
concepts.summary: Polar area uses sectors rather than rectangles, which changes the integrand.

concepts.title: Vector-valued functions
concepts.summary: A vector-valued function traces a curve, and its derivative is a tangent vector.
prerequisites: Motion with parametric and vector functions

concepts.title: Convergence of sequences
concepts.summary: A sequence converges when its terms approach a single finite limit.

concepts.title: Introduction to series
concepts.summary: A series is the sum of a sequence, and its partial sums decide convergence.

concepts.title: Geometric series
concepts.summary: A geometric series converges exactly when the common ratio is smaller than one in size.

concepts.title: The nth-term test
concepts.summary: If the terms do not approach zero, the series diverges, but the converse does not hold.

concepts.title: The integral test
concepts.summary: A series and a related improper integral converge or diverge together.

concepts.title: Comparison tests
concepts.summary: Bounding a series by a known one decides convergence term by term.

concepts.title: The alternating series test
concepts.summary: Alternating terms that decrease to zero converge, with a bounded error.

concepts.title: The ratio test
concepts.summary: The ratio of successive terms decides absolute convergence, especially for factorials and powers.

concepts.title: Absolute and conditional convergence
concepts.summary: A series can converge while the series of absolute values diverges.

concepts.title: Taylor and Maclaurin series
concepts.summary: A smooth function can be represented by a power series built from its derivatives at a point.

concepts.title: Power series and radius of convergence
concepts.summary: A power series converges on an interval whose radius is found from the ratio test.

concepts.title: Approximating functions with polynomials
concepts.summary: A Taylor polynomial approximates a function with a controllable error bound.
prerequisites: Power series and radius of convergence
